chapter: Records, dances and Blanche Calloway (repeated passages)
title: Travelling by bus, train and touring car then and now
summary: Air travel is best now; in the Twenties bands crowded into touring cars with celluloid curtains, bass drum on the back and bad roads.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Has it changed a lot over the years, you know, conditions for traveling and so on...

Well, it certainly has. You know, air travel is the thing now. You get there and you can rest before you do anything. When you traveled by bus, by the time you got in, you had to go to work. You might be late getting in, you know, so that money would be docked from your money. You know? So it's best traveling by air. The train is a tiresome thing, too.
That wasn't too often the case, was it, that a band would go by train?

No, it wasn't. It would have been better, really. It would have been a lot better. Because at least you could get a compartment, and lay down and rest. But if you have to sit up in a train a long while, the sitting is kind of tiresome, too.
I guess the band buses, for instance, in the Twenties were not exactly very (?).

Oh, they were terrible buses. A lot of times we didn't travel by bus in them days. We traveled by touring car. It had celluloid(?) curtains on the windows, you know, and you could put the bass drum on the back tires,
and they had little things on the running boards where you'd put your grips and things. Terrible...!
How many guys would be in a thing like that?

Oh, there would be... They'd try to get a Cadillac if they could; you know, one of them old Cadillacs, or get the big cars so that they could get as many guys in as they could. Maybe seven in one. As many as they could. And then you had to have all your grips in there, the whole bit, and your instruments. Boy, it was something else.
And roads were also not so good then.
Yeah, the roads were bad. It was a real rough time, you know.
